basic_identification.full_title: Room Air Conditioners — Specification: Part 2 Split Air Conditioners (Fourth Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering (finalised by the Mechanical Engineering Department Sectional Committee)

scope.summary: This specific document is a one-page amendment sheet that updates the requirements for refrigerant pipes and fittings of split air conditioners. The base standard covers specifications for split-type room air conditioners, but the full scope is not detailed in this amendment sheet [1].
scope.page_number: Page 1 (amending Page 4 of the base standard)

amendment_slips.description: Substitutes Clause 5.3.1 on Page 4 to mandate that refrigerant pipes and fittings must withstand three times the design pressure of the refrigeration circuit for at least 1 minute (referencing IS 11329) and pass the drift expanding test (referencing IS 10773) [1].

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: N/A
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Provides the baseline pressure test parameters (specifically Clause 7.3.1) to ensure the refrigeration circuit pipes can withstand 3 times the design pressure for at least 1 minute [1].

cross_referenced_standards_top_20.title: N/A
cross_referenced_standards_top_20.relevance: Specifies the test methods and parameters (specifically Clause 8.3) for performing the mandatory drift expanding test on the refrigerant pipes and fittings [1].

certification_and_marking.certification_status: No explicit BIS product certification, ISI Mark, or CRS Registration requirements are mentioned in this 1-page amendment sheet.

plain_language_summary.summary: This document is Amendment No. 1 (May 2026) to the fourth revision of IS 1391 (Part 2) : 2023 for Split Room Air Conditioners [1]. It substitutes the requirements under Clause 5.3.1 to mandate that all integrated refrigerant pipes and fittings must satisfy two critical mechanical tests: a high-pressure tolerance test (withstanding three times the design pressure for a minimum of one minute per IS 11329) and a drift expanding test per IS 10773 [1]. When designing, testing, or auditing split air conditioning units, engineers must verify that piping systems comply with these revised strength and ductility parameters [1].
